Hi Naomi / Ralph — jumping in with the requested breakdown and concrete acceptance criteria. High level first, then sizing scenarios.

Private VPC lead-time breakdown (typical):
- Procurement & capacity reservation (ordering GPU instances or rackspace): 2–4 weeks (depends on tranche availability).
- Networking & peering setup (customer VPC <-> Redwood transit): 1–2 weeks (customer-side firewall rules and peering approvals can add time).
- Security/compliance onboarding (KMS, audit logs, SOC2 docs review): 1–2 weeks (can run in parallel with networking).
- Configuration & validation (model deploy, KV cache priming, routing policies): 1 week.

Realistic ranges: 4–9 weeks end-to-end. If procurement and networking stalls occur, plan for the higher end. The 6–10 week estimate Naomi mentioned is conservative to account for approvals.

Acceptance criteria for 2-week Private VPC evaluation (pass/fail):
- Functional: model endpoints respond to authenticated requests; streaming works with chunked tokens.
- Performance (staging workload mirroring production 20% traffic profile):
  - Throughput: sustained 2,000 requests/hour across endpoints during the busiest hour.
  - Latency: 95th percentile token latency < 300ms for single-session gen up to 1,024 tokens; end-to-end response time for common prompt patterns < 1.2s.
  - Concurrency: support 50 concurrent inference streams with < 5% error rate.
- Quality: BLEU/ROUGE style prompt-specific metrics and a small hand-verified set of 200 prompts should show no more than a 5% drop in baseline quality for key intents.
- Security: end-to-end encryption for KV cache and data-at-rest; audit logs delivered to customer S3/KMS integration.

GPU pool sizing scenarios (A100-equivalent):
1) Conservative (min viable reserve): 8 GPUs — supports initial eval and low-volume production (burst to hosted). Recommended when you want fast time-to-first-traffic and can rely on burst capacity. Cost: baseline X (see attached spreadsheet).
2) Expected (recommended initial reserve): 16 GPUs — balanced for continuous traffic 10k–30k requests/day with 95th p99 latency targets intact. Good fit for Medicore mid-Q1 growth.
3) Aggressive (high availability): 32 GPUs — for higher throughput and redundancy across AZs; useful if you plan to keep model variants and active A/B routing.

Notes on quantization & cost: mixing int8 quantized variants on lower-cost GPUs can reduce unit cost by ~30–40% at modest quality trade-offs; we can propose a hybrid pool (12 high-precision + 4 quantized) if cost is a constraint.

Attachments I’m sharing here: GPU_Sizing_Scenarios.xlsx (detailed cost bands and expected tokens/sec per model), SOC2-summary.pdf (security checklist we’ll need to verify).

If you want I can sketch a staged acceptance checklist that the SREs can run as a post-deploy smoke test (we can add the curl/snippet checks).

— Marissa

Ralph / Lena — thanks for the quick turnaround and excellent questions. Per Marissa’s breakdown, here’s a concrete next-steps MAP we recommend if Medicore wants to hold the mid-June PO cutoff and hit a late-Q3 go-live:

1) PO & Reservation (by 2027-06-14): commit to the 16 GPU initial reserve (DEAL-7862 pricing band).
2) Security & Docs (parallel, Week 0–1): sign NDA addendum, provide SOC2 scoping info (we’ll push the SOC2-summary.pdf and KMS integration checklist).
3) Provisioning (Week 1–4): procurement + network peering + basic config.
4) Eval Window (2 weeks, Week 5–6): Private VPC staging run with automated smoke tests (Marissa will provide the checklist). Pass criteria: Marissa’s perf/security/quality bullets above.
5) Acceptance & Go-Live (Week 7): if eval passes, convert reserve to production pool and schedule live cutover during agreed maintenance window.

Decision points and remedies: if any acceptance criteria fail, we’ll triage and provide two options — (A) allow a 1-week remediation window with targeted fixes, or (B) fallback to a canary production on hosted API while we remediate the Private VPC.

Deliverables for you this week: updated MAP (signed-ready PDF), a one-page acceptance checklist for SRE, and a DocuSign link for the PO/reservation term sheet. Can you confirm: (a) you have internal procurement cadence to hit June 14, and (b) whether your SREs prefer the conservative (8 GPU) or expected (16 GPU) starting pool?

If you’re comfortable, we’ll generate the DocuSign and schedule a 30-minute kickoff next Tuesday to walk through the acceptance checklist with your SREs.
